title: Secondary Air Injection System Air Flow/Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic Bank 2
plain: The signal from the secondary air injection pressure sensor (bank 2) keeps dropping out or jumping around. This sensor checks that the air pump is blowing fresh air into the exhaust during cold starts. A loose connection or a damaged wire is the usual reason.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Chafed wire that opens or shorts as the engine moves
Failing secondary air injection pressure sensor

checks: Wiggle the harness and connector while watching live data for dropouts
Inspect the secondary air sensor wiring along its whole route
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the secondary air injection pressure sensor.

cost.job: Replace secondary air injection pressure sensor

title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Open Bank 1
plain: The valve that lets fresh air from the secondary air pump into the exhaust on bank 1 (the side of the engine with cylinder 1) seems stuck open. This system only runs for a short time after a cold start.
symptoms: Possible loud whine or roar from the air pump after a cold start
Some vehicles go into limp mode

causes.name: Moisture or corrosion inside the valve

checks: Check whether air flows through the valve when it should be closed or open
Inspect the valve and hoses for water damage or corrosion
fix: Replace the stuck switching valve; water-damaged pumps often need replacing too.
examples: Known on Toyota Tundra and Sequoia V8s and some Lexus models with secondary air injection

title: Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck On Bank 1
plain: The secondary air pump, which blows fresh air into the exhaust for a short time after cold starts, seems stuck on. This code is for bank 1, the side of the engine with cylinder 1.
symptoms: Air pump keeps running or whining after start-up

causes.name: Stuck switching valve or faulty pressure sensor

checks: Check the air pump fuse and relay
Listen for the pump at a cold start and check that it shuts off
fix: Replace the failed pump, relay or valve and repair any wiring fault.
examples: Known on Toyota Tundra and Sequoia V8s and some Lexus models with secondary air injection

title: Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck Off Bank 1
plain: The secondary air pump, which blows fresh air into the exhaust for a short time after cold starts, seems stuck off. This code is for bank 1, the side of the engine with cylinder 1.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Failed secondary air pump (often water damaged)
Blown fuse or failed pump relay
Stuck switching valve or faulty pressure sensor

checks: Check the air pump fuse and relay
Listen for the pump at a cold start and check that it shuts off
fix: Replace the failed pump, relay or valve and repair any wiring fault.

title: Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck On Bank 2
plain: The secondary air pump, which blows fresh air into the exhaust for a short time after cold starts, seems stuck on. This code is for bank 2, the side of the engine without cylinder 1.
symptoms: Air pump keeps running or whining after start-up

causes.name: Stuck switching valve or faulty pressure sensor

checks: Check the air pump fuse and relay
Listen for the pump at a cold start and check that it shuts off
fix: Replace the failed pump, relay or valve and repair any wiring fault.

title: Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck Off Bank 2

title: Secondary Air Injection System High Airflow Bank 1
plain: More air than expected is flowing through the secondary air system on bank 1 (the side of the engine with cylinder 1), often from a leak in the air hoses or exhaust after the valve.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Disconnected or cracked secondary air hose
Leak at the switching valve or exhaust connection

checks: Inspect secondary air hoses and valve connections
Compare air pressure readings with the pump running
fix: Repair the leak or replace the faulty valve or sensor.

cost.job: Replace secondary air hose or valve

title: Secondary Air Injection System High Airflow Bank 2

Leak at the switching valve or exhaust connection

fix: Repair the leak or replace the faulty valve or sensor.

title: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Too Low Bank 1
plain: The pressure difference across the diesel particulate filter is lower than it should be. The filter may be cracked, or the pressure sensor or its hoses may be faulty.

causes.name: Cracked, disconnected or leaking DPF pressure sensor hose

checks: Inspect the DPF pressure sensor hoses
Compare DPF pressure readings at idle and higher RPM
fix: Repair the hoses or sensor; replace the filter if it is cracked.

title: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Too High Bank 1
plain: The pressure difference across the diesel particulate filter is higher than it should be, meaning the filter is clogged or the sensor is misreading.

causes.name: Filter clogged with soot or ash

checks: Check DPF pressure readings and soot load with a scan tool
Inspect sensor hoses and run a forced regeneration if allowed
fix: Run a forced regeneration; if that doesn't clear it, clean or replace the filter or sensor.

cost.job: Forced DPF regeneration or filter cleaning

title: Evaporative Emission System Switching Valve Performance/Stuck Open
plain: The EVAP switching valve isn't working as expected and may be stuck open. The fuel vapor system can't route or seal vapor properly.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Dirt or debris in the valve

checks: Command the valve with a scan tool and check that it opens and closes
Inspect the EVAP hoses around the valve
fix: Replace the switching valve and repair any damaged hoses.

title: Evaporative Emission System Switching Valve Stuck Closed
plain: The EVAP switching valve seems stuck closed, so fuel vapor can't flow where it should.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
checks: Command the valve with a scan tool and check that it opens
Check the lines on both sides of the valve for blockage
fix: Replace the stuck valve and clear any blocked lines.

title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit
plain: The engine computer has found a problem in the circuit for the diesel particulate filter (DPF) pressure sensor, which measures pressure across the diesel particulate filter to tell how full of soot it is. It usually points to wiring, a connector or the sensor itself.
symptoms: Filter cleaning (regeneration) may run too often or not at all
checks: Inspect the DPF pressure sensor connector and wiring for damage or corrosion
Check the sensor power, ground and signal with a meter
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the DPF differential pressure sensor.

title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The diesel particulate filter (DPF) pressure sensor is giving readings that don't make sense compared with what the computer expects. This sensor measures pressure across the diesel particulate filter to tell how full of soot it is. The sensor may be failing or the system it watches may have a real problem.
symptoms: Filter cleaning (regeneration) may run too often or not at all

causes.name: Failing or out-of-calibration DPF differential pressure sensor
Cracked, loose or soot-plugged sensor hoses
High resistance in the wiring or connector

checks: Compare the DPF pressure sensor reading with related sensors in live data
Check wiring and connector for corrosion or looseness
fix: Confirm the system itself is working, then replace the DPF differential pressure sensor if its readings are off.

title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit Low
plain: The signal from the diesel particulate filter (DPF) pressure sensor is lower than the computer expects. This sensor measures pressure across the diesel particulate filter to tell how full of soot it is. A wire shorted to ground or a failed sensor is the usual reason.
symptoms: Filter cleaning (regeneration) may run too often or not at all

causes.name: Signal or reference wire shorted to ground

checks: Inspect the DPF pressure sensor wiring for rubbed-through or pinched spots
Unplug the sensor and see if the reading changes, which helps separate wiring from sensor
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the DPF differential pressure sensor.

title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit High
plain: The signal from the diesel particulate filter (DPF) pressure sensor is higher than the computer expects. This sensor measures pressure across the diesel particulate filter to tell how full of soot it is. An open (broken) wire, a bad ground or a failed sensor is the usual reason.
symptoms: Filter cleaning (regeneration) may run too often or not at all

causes.name: Open or broken signal or ground wire
Wire shorted to a power source

checks: Make sure the DPF pressure sensor connector is fully plugged in and clean
Check the sensor ground and signal wire for an open circuit
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the DPF differential pressure sensor.

title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
plain: The signal from the diesel particulate filter (DPF) pressure sensor keeps dropping out or jumping around. This sensor measures pressure across the diesel particulate filter to tell how full of soot it is. A loose connection or a damaged wire is the usual reason.
symptoms: Filter cleaning (regeneration) may run too often or not at all

causes.name: Chafed wire that opens or shorts as the engine moves

checks: Wiggle the harness and connector while watching live data for dropouts
Inspect the DPF pressure sensor wiring along its whole route
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the DPF differential pressure sensor.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Cooling System Performance
plain: The EGR cooler, which cools exhaust gas before it's fed back into a diesel engine, isn't cooling it as much as it should. It is often clogged with soot.
symptoms: Possible white smoke or coolant loss if the cooler leaks

causes.name: Low coolant or weak coolant flow

checks: Compare EGR temperature readings before and after the cooler
Check coolant level and look for coolant loss
fix: Clean or replace the clogged EGR cooler and fix any stuck bypass valve.
examples: Known on Ford Power Stroke 6.4L and 6.7L diesel pickups

title: Diesel Particulate Filter Regeneration Duration
plain: The diesel particulate filter's self-cleaning burn (regeneration) took longer than it should have to finish.

causes.name: Lots of short trips that interrupt regeneration
Faulty DPF pressure sensor or hoses
Leaking injector or engine problem making extra soot

checks: Check DPF pressure and exhaust temperature readings in live data
Take a long highway drive or run a service regeneration
fix: Fix any sensor faults, then run a forced regeneration; clean or replace the filter if it won't clear.

cost.job: Forced DPF regeneration or sensor replacement

title: Diesel Particulate Filter Regeneration Frequency
plain: The diesel particulate filter is needing to clean itself (regenerate) more often than it should. Something is making extra soot, or the sensors are misreading how full it is.
symptoms: Frequent regeneration cycles (higher idle, fan running, hot smell)

causes.name: Faulty DPF pressure sensor or cracked sensor hoses
Engine making too much soot (injector or EGR problem)
Ash buildup in an older filter
Lots of short trips or long idling

checks: Check DPF pressure sensor hoses and readings
Check for other engine codes that could cause extra soot
fix: Repair the sensor or the source of extra soot; an ash-loaded filter may need cleaning or replacing.
examples: Seen on GM Duramax diesel pickups

title: Diesel Particulate Filter Restriction - Soot Accumulation
plain: The diesel particulate filter is too full of soot. The engine may limit power until the filter is cleaned by a regeneration.
symptoms: DPF full or regeneration needed message

causes.name: Too many short trips so regeneration never completes
Faulty DPF pressure sensor or plugged sensor hoses
Engine making extra soot (injector, EGR or turbo problem)
Faulty exhaust temperature sensor stopping regeneration

checks: Check for other codes that block regeneration
Run a forced regeneration with a scan tool
Check DPF pressure sensor hoses for soot plugging
fix: Fix whatever stopped regeneration, then run a forced regeneration; replace or clean the filter if it won't clear.

cost.job: Forced DPF regeneration or filter cleaning

examples: Well known on GM Duramax diesel pickups
